html:
The Peacock Throne was the jeweled throne of the Mughal emperors, ordered by Shah Jahan and finished in 1635, in the palace at Delhi.

It was a platform of gold and silver covered with gems, with a canopy and figures of peacocks with spread tails. The Koh-i-Noor diamond was set into it. Contemporaries valued it as worth more than the Taj Mahal, which Shah Jahan began shortly before.

In 1739 Nader Shah of Persia took Delhi and carried the throne away to Iran as the greatest prize of his campaign. It was probably broken up after his death. Later Persian rulers used a throne of the same name, which is not the original.
sum: The Peacock Throne was the jeweled throne of the Mughal emperors, ordered by Shah Jahan and finished in 1635, in the palace at Delhi.
